messages.subject: selecting residuals Lavaan
parts:
Hello,

I have used the LavResiduals function with my CFA model. The output looks fine but how can I select only those residuals above a certain value? My correlation matrix is too large to oversee it all. I've tried: 
 a <- lavResiduals(myfitmodel))
a[["cov"]]>0.20

This returns the whole matrix with the corresponding TRUE/FALSE values. But I just want to see the TRUE values of even better the only the actual values of the pairs that exceed >0.20 in my case.

Hope someone van help me out

cheers, G.

messages.author: 17944621d521fdfa
messages.subject: Re: selecting residuals Lavaan
parts:
Hi Guido,

I am not sure if Lavaan has an argument for that. But I did have the same issue and this is what I've done:

residual_order<-resid(fit, "cor")$cov
cov_tibble <- tibble(variables = NA, cov = NA)
for (rowname in rownames(residual_order)) {
  for (colname in colnames(residual_order)) {
    cov_tibble %<>%
      rbind(
        tibble(variables = paste(rownames(residual_order)[which(rownames(residual_order) == rowname)],
                                 colnames(residual_order)[which(colnames(residual_order) == colname)]),
               cov = residual_order[rownames(residual_order)[which(rownames(residual_order) == rowname)],
                                    colnames(residual_order)[which(colnames(residual_order) == colname)]]) 
      )
  }
}
cov_tibble %<>% {.[-1, ]} %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(cov)))


You will find a new object called "cov_tibble" with the arranged values in descending order. Hope it helps :) 


Fran

messages.subject: Re: selecting residuals Lavaan
parts:
thx! I've just found another work around that is even easier:

library(caret)

over20 <-findCorrelation(a, cutoff = 0.20, names = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)  # with the verbose = TRUE it shows which rows and columns have corr >.20 including the corresponding value

With the following commands it is easy to look up te corresponding values
over20 # the corresponding variable names are shown
rownames(a) # look up the positions of the variabel names and combine this info with the first step by just looking

colnames(a) (these are in fact the same as the rownames of course, so this step is not really neccesary)
